choice.title: Pondside @PONDSIDE_VERSION@
choice.description: The Pondside app, installed in Applications.

choice.title: LilyPond @LILYPOND_VERSION@
choice.description: The engraver Pondside runs on every edit. Required. This is the version Pondside is tested with; a LilyPond you already have is still used for scores that declare its version.

choice.title: Command-line tool
choice.description: Links the pondside command (CLI and MCP server for agents) into /usr/local/bin.

choice.title: FluidSynth @FLUIDSYNTH_VERSION@ and a General MIDI SoundFont
choice.description: Renders an audio mockup of the score when MuseScore is not installed. About 35 MB.

choice.title: SuperCollider engine @SUPERCOLLIDER_VERSION@ (headless)
choice.description: The SuperCollider language and audio server without its IDE, for live electronics, patches and the mix. About 16 MB.

choice.title: SuperCollider @SUPERCOLLIDER_VERSION@ (with its IDE)
choice.description: For live-electronics scores: Pondside writes cue times and pitch collections for SuperCollider patches. Downloaded from the SuperCollider project during installation (about 240 MB). Unticked if SuperCollider is already in Applications.

choice.title: MuseScore Studio @MUSESCORE_VERSION@
choice.description: Optional, higher-quality audio mockups. Downloaded from MuseScore during installation (about 200 MB). Muse Sounds instruments are installed separately through Muse Hub.

choice.title: Claude Code @CLAUDE_VERSION@ (agent)
choice.description: A coding agent for Pondside's agent features: describe a change to a graphic (⌘L), and finish SuperCollider patch migrations unattended. Installed into your home folder by Anthropic's own install script; needs an Anthropic account or API key (run claude once to sign in). Pick it in Pondside ▸ Settings.

choice.title: opencode @OPENCODE_VERSION@ (agent)
choice.description: An open-source coding agent, as an alternative to Claude Code, for the same features. Installed into your home folder by opencode's own install script; needs a model provider (run opencode once to set one up).
